entries.claim: The persisted forge answers are interpolated as unquoted shell prose, although both `owner/name` and the Forgejo host are open-ended user-controlled answers and are not validated by `forge.mjs`.
entries.failure_scenario: A user (or text copied from an untrusted repository/instruction) supplies `org/repo; rm -rf "$HOME"` for the repository field. The prescribed command becomes `... config.mjs set git.forge_provider=github git.forge_repo=org/repo; rm -rf "$HOME"`, so the shell executes the suffix. The Forgejo-only `git.forge_host=<host>` interpolation has the same vulnerability. `isForgeSlug` only filters an origin-derived default; it is never applied to the answer this workflow persists.

counter_evidence.note: The blocker rests on a third party controlling the interpolated value, and no path gives them one. Every value that is NOT typed by the user at the ask-user seam is already validated: new-project.md:105 pre-fills the slug from `defaults.repo`, which is `originDefaults()` at cadence-core/bin/lib/forge-decision.mjs:240 - `repo: isForgeSlug(c.slug) ? c.slug : null` - so an origin-derived slug from a hostile clone is filtered by the very function the finding says is never applied, and forge-decision.test.mjs:230 asserts it refuses every character that could end an argument. The Forgejo host is never pre-filled at all (new-project.md:108, "with NO default offered"), so it is always the user typing at their own prompt. cadence-core/references/conventions.md:136 classifies exactly that case: "The inline form also stays for a human typing at a shell, where the text is the user’s own to begin with." What survives the two overstatements is real but smaller: an ACCEPTED typed answer is never shape-checked, so a malformed slug persists and phase 2 acts on it. Downgraded to medium and filed as an open item.

entries.claim: The adopt entry point repeats the unquoted interpolation of user-provided forge repository and host values into a shell command.
entries.failure_scenario: Selecting Forgejo and entering a host such as `forge.example; rm -rf .planning` causes the documented persistence invocation to execute the injected command after `config.mjs set`. Entering a malicious repository slug has the same effect. The stated refusal before persistence only covers selecting "None of these"; it does not validate accepted open-ended answers.

counter_evidence.note: Same defect and same counter-evidence as the new-project.md finding - adopt.md:125-130 is the identical persist block, and adopt.md reaches it through the same `forge.mjs detect` envelope whose slug default passes through isForgeSlug at forge-decision.mjs:240. The host in the cited scenario is user-typed with no default offered (adopt.md:100-103), which conventions.md:136 classifies as inline-by-rule rather than caller-derived text. Downgraded to medium, merged with the finding above as one open item.
